newsitem.title: UK: Palm oil lower, dlr supports soft oils in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Palm oil lower, dlr supports soft oils in Europe.

text.p: Palm oil ended lower on Tuesday on the European vegetable oil market following the easier close in Malaysia while a firm dollar underpinned soft oils.
Palm oil futures finished lower in Kuala Lumpur on profit-taking and liquidation as demand from refiners dried up on the physical market.
Traders in Europe said the fall in Malaysia was enough to halt trading in palm oil.
"People want to see what will happen on Wednesday before they commit themselves," said one trader.
At the close crude palm oil cif Europe was $2.50 to $5 down after May traded at $560 a tonne cif.
Among products RBD palm oil was unchanged to $5 down while olein was $2.50 lower with no further business reported.
Lauric oils followed the easier trend in palm oil and close with coconut and palmkernel oil $2.50 down.
A firm dollar countered easier futures in Chicago and prices in Europe finished with Dutch soy oil 0.50 to one guilders up after May traded at 104 guilders a 100 kilos.
Dutch/EU rape oil closed unchanged to 0.50 guilders higher after May/Jul traded at 104.75 and Aug/Oct at 104 and 103.75 guilders a 100 kilos fob ex-mill.
